pages.title: The Building
pages.content:
Warehouse No. 7, 1924

The Building

Warehouse No. 7 was built in 1924 on Kessel Quay to store coffee and rope. Henrik Lund’s team repaired the brick façade bay by bay between 2016 and 2019.

pages.title: Rooms & Rates
pages.content:
32 rooms

Rooms & Rates

Harbour Room €210, Quay Double €260, Loft Suite €380 and Crane Suite €540 per night. Breakfast at the Canteen is €24 per person; late check-out until 15:00 is €40.

pages.title: People
pages.content:
Who runs the building

People

Ines Varga, Tomas Adeyemi, Mirela Costa, Henrik Lund, Noor Haddad, Lucía Ferro and Pavel Novak rebuilt and now run Soko Hotel.

pages.title: The Canteen
pages.content:
Breakfast and dinner

The Canteen

Breakfast daily 07:00–10:30 for €24 per person; dinner Wednesday to Sunday 18:00–22:00. Noor Haddad leads the kitchen.

Visit

Pier 7, Kessel Quay 14, Vessa Harbour. Arrive at Door 7 on the quay; reception is behind it and open 24 hours. Check-in 15:00, check-out 11:00.

posts.title: The Brick Count
posts.excerpt: How Henrik Lund and his masons restored the warehouse façade bay by bay with salvaged brick.
posts.content:
When the restoration began in 2016, master mason Henrik Lund did not order new bricks. The façade of Warehouse No. 7 was repaired one arched bay at a time, and wherever a brick had failed it was replaced with one salvaged from the collapsed loading shed beside the building.

Every bay was counted before work started: the sound bricks, the cracked ones, the ones that could be turned and reused. Henrik’s team cleaned and pointed each wall by hand, working under a single lamp on low scaffolding so the old mortar could be matched by eye.

The work took three years. Today the wall you see from the quay is the same wall that was raised in 1924, with its repairs left visible, the way a good mend should be.

posts.title: The Crane Beam
posts.excerpt: Why the riveted iron crane beam stayed in place above the two top-floor suites.
posts.content:
High under the roof of Warehouse No. 7 an iron beam once carried a hoist that lifted sacks and cordage from the quay. When Ines Varga drew the conversion, she kept it exactly where it was.

The beam now runs across the ceiling of both Crane Suites, riveted, dark and slightly bowed. A freestanding bath stands beneath it by the window, and the harbour lies beyond.

Nothing was added to the beam and nothing was taken away. It is the one object in the hotel that still does the work it was built for: it holds the building up.

posts.title: The Night Log
posts.excerpt: Pavel Novak’s handwritten record of ships, weather and late arrivals.
posts.content:
Behind Door 7 the night porter, Pavel Novak, keeps a notebook. Each night he writes down the ships that pass, the weather on the water and anyone who arrives after midnight.

The log is handwritten and kept at the reception desk. Guests are welcome to read it at breakfast, and many do.

On a quiet night the entry may be a single line: wind from the north, one tug, nobody late.
